Confirmed the pi-durable 1.5.0 mechanics by reading its dist source: `abortConversation` (scheduler.js:449-473) marks tasks *and* calls `withdrawQueuedInputs` (inbox.js:113-122) — the withdrawal this PR avoids; `#reconcile`'s withdrawal (scheduler.js:857) fires only below a cancelled *task owner* (`#belowCancelled`, :1543), so per-task aborts leave the root inbox intact while subagent inboxes still cascade; the abort handler ends the run without touching the inbox (generation.js:263-288); `continue` places queued items first only when the conversation is idle and throws `ConversationBusy` otherwise (submissions.js:204-213), which is why `startQueued` checks `LiveDoc.run` in the same commit; `afterFailedRun` defaults to `"keep"` (agent.js:60) and quack does not override it, so a failed next run would still park its inputs.

Checked the distributor's invariant holds on the new path: `NOT_FORWARDED` already strips a client-sent `x-quack-principal` on main (packages/distributor/src/server.ts:90), so forwarding the proxy's own copy on the upgrade is consistent with HTTP; session-listener callers reach the route with `who === undefined` (server.ts:570), so their aborts log as `service` as described.

Traced the sender's resume logic against the store's semantics: a 409's lower `acked` is committed and the batch re-sent from there, which is contiguous because the stream is append-only; the no-progress case (a refused spend holding the watermark) waits instead of looping. Both paths have tests (`a reset catalog is refilled from the log`, and the store's `holds` rule for spend).
